Spectral gaps and explicit Fourier distributions

Reconstructed and self-checked by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), Ultra reasoning effort, October 2026. Earlier edition: GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI), Ultra reasoning effort. Original exposition: CC0. Supplied foundations retain their stated licences.

A Fourier derivative equation can lose a point mass at zero. We calculate complete distributions, keeping the masses, their derivatives and the precise finite parts. We then prove the norm identities used in the examples and construct the unique bounded primitive with no frequency near zero.

Use , , and . Pairings are bilinear. The supplied Fourier foundation, F1–F5, proves every Schwartz estimate, inversion, coordinate identity and transpose convention. U041, Lemma 0.1, proves Schwartz Parseval from absolute Fubini and that inversion. U040, Lemma 2.1, proves the global convolution multiplier identity. U045, Solution 2, proves the Cauchy Fourier pair by elementary Laplace integration and Fourier inversion.

The scalar foundation, Sections 12.4–12.9, 13.1–13.5 and 13.7–13.10, supplies compactness, FTC, trigonometry and cutoffs. The integration foundation, Sections 15.0–15.4 and 16.1–16.2, supplies convergence, Fubini, Cauchy–Schwarz, completeness and mollification. We prove the pole limits and the classification of all primitives here.

The complete integral Taylor proof supplies the finite-order remainders used here, including signed increments, complex-valued functions, directional derivatives and uniform bounds for all required derivatives on compact neighborhoods.
